scientific_integrity: The ordinary infinite-divisibility classification is historical prior work of Letac, Malouche and Maurer (2002), not claimed as new. The evaluated contribution is the separate sharp binomial-thinning and log-concavity criteria; 2021 real-power paper full text unavailable, so historical-priority risk is documented.
scientific_limitations: Classification requires independent summands, positive real NB shape and strictly interior Bernoulli and NB probabilities; no statement about multivariate or ordinary real-line self-decomposability. Finite rational diagnostics are not proofs. Earlier equivalent formulations remain a residual historical-priority risk.
title: Sharp thinning and log-concavity boundaries for Bernoulli–negative-binomial counts
